NITI Aayog Convenes Regional Best Practices Seminar (South) under Aspirational District and Block Programme! The Regional Best Practices Seminar (South) under the Aspirational Districts and Blocks Programme (ADP/ABP) was conducted today at Visakhapatnam, bringing together District Collectors, State officials and development practitioners from across southern states to showcase innovative governance practices and accelerate district transformation. Shri Rohit Kumar, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, ADP/ABP, NITI Aayog, in his keynote address provided an overview of the Aspirational Districts and Blocks Programme and appreciated the sustained efforts of District administrations, Block officials and frontline functionaries in driving development outcomes on the ground. He emphasised that the programme should evolve into a Jan Andolan, with strong community participation and convergence across departments. He also noted that a majority of the programme indicators are nearing saturation in several districts and appreciated the strong performance of southern states under the ADP/ABP framework. Delivering the Special Address, Shri Anant Shankar, Joint Secretary, Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, highlighted the State’s focus on removing absolute poverty through targeted initiatives including the Zero Poverty Mission, guided by the vision of P4 – Public, Private, People Partnerships. He also noted the steady progress made by Andhra Pradesh and other southern states across key development indicators under the programme. The event also witnessed the unveiling of the Best Practices Compendium, showcasing impactful initiatives from districts across southern India that are improving outcomes in Education, Healthcare, Nutrition and Livelihoods. District Collectors and senior officers from Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands presented innovative district-level initiatives and participated in discussions on scaling best practices, strengthening convergence and improving last-mile service delivery. The seminar reaffirmed the importance of knowledge sharing, district-led innovation and collaborative governance in accelerating progress across Aspirational Districts and Blocks. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #AspirationalDistricts #AspirationalBlocks #BestPractices #ADP #ABP #DistrictTransformation #CooperativeFederalism #DataDrivenGovernance #TransformingIndia

It’s a tomahawk, end of. Matt Tardio (@angertab) The evidence is clear, this is not a Tomahawk Iran alleged that an American Tomahawk Cruise Missile hit a school (buried in an IRGC compound) in southern Iran, killing 165 people. Analysis of a newly released video tells a different story. ANALYSIS: A-I analysis confirms the wings of the munition in question sit about 40%-45% down the body of the munition. On a Tomahawk, the wings sit roughly 49%-50% down the body of the munition. The wing to body ratio of the munition in question matches an Iranian Kh-55–derived Land Attack Cruise Missile. Further, the video shows the munition in a steep dive angle for the final attack phase. This places the attack angle at approximately 70%, which is the max attack angle for a Tomahawk. The attack angle does not match the KH-55. That angle maxes out at about 55 degrees. So what would have caused this? CONCLUSION: The wing positioning alone makes the munition impossible to be a Tomahawk. The attack angle is at the max of the Tomahawk's capabilities. The typical attack angle for a Tomahawk is much lower than 70 degrees. The typical angle is between 20-45 degrees. This is due to the flight pattern of Tomahawks. They fly very low horizontally to the ground, often only 50-100 meters AGL to avoid detection and interception. In order to achieve that attack angle, the missile would have had to gain altitude several kilometers away, this would leave it vulnerable for interception. This is highly unlikely on the first day of US attacks. So what could have caused this? Simply put, GPS jamming of an Iranian KH-55. The USA and Israel were, and continue to actively jam the Iranian airspace. If the KH-55's signal was jammed, this could result in an uncontrollable dive. Think of GPS jamming more like disorienting the missile. UNA DE CADA SEIS PERSONAS OPERADAS POR CÁNCER COLORRECTAL EN ARGENTINA TIENE MENOS DE 50 AÑOS Un estudio del Consorcio Argentino de Cáncer Colorrectal, publicado en The Lancet Regional Health Americas, analizó a 1.829 pacientes operados en 32 hospitales de 10 provincias argentinas entre abril de 2022 y diciembre de 2023. La investigación detectó que uno de cada seis pacientes intervenidos tenía menos de 50 años y, en este grupo, la mayoría no presentaba antecedentes familiares ni síndromes hereditarios. En los menores de 50 años, el 18% tenía metástasis al momento de la cirugía y los tumores se localizaron principalmente en el recto. La frecuencia de metástasis en pacientes jóvenes duplicó a la de los casos de inicio tardío. El estudio sugiere revisar la edad para iniciar los controles, aunque los autores reconocen que se requieren más investigaciones para actualizar las guías nacionales. Infobae 🔗infob.ae/4rhsHbd

JUST IN: The MarineTraffic timelapse tells one story. The reality tells another. On screen, the Strait of Hormuz has gone dark. Traffic collapsed 80 to 95% from a normal 40 to 60 tankers per day to single digits. The timelapse shows a waterway that carried 20% of global oil supply reduced to a near-empty corridor. Brent surged past $119 on the visual evidence of a chokepoint shutdown. But the Strait is not empty. It is invisible. Ships are crossing. They turn off their AIS transponders before entry, transit in darkness, and reactivate on the other side. Others spoof their identity entirely: broadcasting fake vessel names, false positions, or “CHINA OWNER” on their Automatic Identification System to exploit Iran’s selective exemption for Chinese-linked vessels. The bulk carriers Iron Maiden and Sino Ocean transited by claiming Chinese status. The sanctioned tanker Danuta I went completely dark, vanished from every tracking platform, and reappeared days later inside the Gulf. The Strait is not closed. It is operating in a shadow state where the only vessels moving are those willing to become invisible to do so. This is worse than closure for the insurance market. And here is why. War-risk actuaries price coverage using AIS-derived data: vessel positions, transit frequency, incident density per nautical mile. When 80 to 95% of traffic disappears from AIS, the models do not see an empty strait. They see a data void. They cannot calculate incident probability in a void. They cannot estimate exposure in a corridor where the vessels that are moving have deliberately erased themselves from the only tracking system insurers rely on. The vessels going dark are not reducing risk. They are destroying the data that would allow risk to be priced. Every transponder switched off before Hormuz entry removes a data point that actuaries need to model safe-transit probability. Every spoofed signal injects false data that corrupts the models from the other direction. The reinsurance market is not merely facing elevated risk. It is facing a measurement crisis where the instruments it depends on have been deliberately sabotaged by the ships using them. War-risk premiums have surged from 0.125% to between 1% and 3% of hull value. Capacity has contracted 60%. Seven P&I clubs covering 90% of global tonnage cancelled war-risk extensions. And the AIS spoofing that enables shadow fleet transits ensures those cancellations cannot be reversed, because the data that would demonstrate safe-transit conditions does not exist. The vessels that could prove the Strait is navigable are the same vessels erasing themselves from the record. Windward, Kpler, and Lloyd’s List Intelligence now fuse satellite imagery, synthetic aperture radar, RF geolocation, and behavioural anomaly scoring to detect dark and spoofed vessels. Over 1,100 vessels were flagged for GNSS manipulation in the Gulf in a single 24-hour period. But detection is not the same as insurability. Knowing a vessel went dark does not make the transit insurable. It makes it documented proof that the transit corridor is ungoverned. The timelapse shows an empty strait. The satellites show ghost ships. The actuaries see neither and cannot price what they cannot measure. The Strait is not closed by missiles. It is not closed by mines. It is closed by the absence of data. Full analysis here ! 👇 open.substack.com/pub/shanak… Video HFI Research (@HFI_Research) Strait of Hormuz in the last 24 hours. BREAKING: The United States has intercepted an encrypted radio transmission believed to originate in Iran that federal agencies assess may serve as an “operational trigger” for sleeper assets pre-positioned outside the country. The transmission was relayed across multiple countries shortly after the killing of Supreme Leader Khamenei on 28 February. It was not sent via internet or cellular networks. It was sent via shortwave radio with encryption keys held only by the intended recipients. A federal alert reviewed by ABC News was distributed to law enforcement agencies across the country on 9 March. It instructs agencies to monitor for suspicious radio frequency signals. The language is precise: “preliminary signals analysis” of an encoded transmission “likely of Iranian origin” intended to “impart instructions” to “clandestine recipients.” Read that again. Not internet. Not phones. Not apps. Radio. The oldest, most deniable, most interception-resistant communication method in the intelligence playbook. The same method numbers stations have used since the Cold War to activate agents who carry nothing but a shortwave receiver and a one-time pad. This is the Mosaic doctrine going global. Inside Iran, the IRGC’s 31 autonomous provincial commands have pre-delegated firing authority to sustain military operations without central leadership. Outside Iran, the IRGC-Quds Force has spent decades pre-positioning assets across the United States, Europe, Latin America, and Africa. Over 20 foiled plots involving Iranian sleeper operatives have been documented since the 2010s by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies and the Atlantic Council. Post-Soleimani in 2020, the FBI disrupted assassination plots against former officials on American soil directed by Quds Force handlers. Hezbollah’s external operations unit maintains dormant cells across Latin America and Western Europe that share infrastructure with Iranian intelligence. These assets do not need the internet. They do not need functioning Iranian embassies. They do not need instructions from a Supreme Leader who is dead or a successor who is wounded and in hiding. They need a radio signal and a pre-agreed code. The federal alert suggests that signal may have been sent. The implications rewrite the geographic boundaries of the war. The conflict was framed as a Middle Eastern air campaign lasting four to six weeks. Eleven days in, the US has closed consulates across 14 countries, evacuated 17,500 citizens, suspended services inside a NATO ally, and is now issuing domestic law enforcement alerts about Iranian activation signals intercepted on American soil. The war’s perimeter has expanded from the Persian Gulf to the American homeland in less than two weeks. The IRGC does not need to penetrate US air defences or launch missiles at American cities. It needs one operative with instructions to damage a pipeline, disrupt a port, attack a diplomatic target, or conduct a high-profile assassination. The asymmetric cost ratio that governs the drone war in the Gulf, $20,000 Shaheds against $4 million interceptors, has a domestic equivalent: one pre-positioned asset with a shortwave radio against the entire US law enforcement and counterintelligence apparatus. The encrypted signal was sent. The alert has been issued. The question is no longer whether the Mosaic doctrine can project force beyond Iran’s borders. The question is whether it already has. Investing in rural women is a trillion-dollar opportunity. Women are central to rural economies - as farmers, entrepreneurs and leaders. Yet they continue to face significant structural barriers to land, finance and markets. Women make up 41% of the global agrifood workforce, contributing across the entire value chain from production to processing and marketing. Yet less than 15% of global landholders are women, limiting their ability to fully participate in and benefit from rural economic growth. Closing these gaps is not only a matter of equality, but also a powerful economic opportunity. Evidence shows that investing in rural women could raise incomes for 58 million people and strengthen resilience for 235 million more. At @IFAD, we invest where impact is greatest: at the #FirstMile of food systems. By expanding access to finance, technology, knowledge and markets, we are helping rural women strengthen livelihoods, build businesses and drive transformation across rural economies. On #InternationalWomensDay, the message is clear: investing in rural women strengthens food systems, economies and global resilience. STATEHOUSE PRESS RELEASE ATTORNEY-GENERAL: RESOLUTION OF THE OPL 245 DISPUTE REPOSITIONS NIGERIA'S ECONOMY, HAILS PRESIDENT TINUBU'S LEADERSHIP The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, has said that resolving the longstanding dispute over OPL 245 will reposition the economy and strengthen the country's fiscal muscle. He praised President Bola Tinubu's visionary leadership, which enabled the breakthrough. The Attorney-General and Minister of Justice, who spoke after the signing of the legal agreement that brought the dispute to an end in Abuja, described the development as a milestone in repositioning Nigeria’s economic landscape. “The agreement marks a turning point for Nigeria’s oil and gas sector after more than two decades of legal battles and international arbitration,” he said. The federal government reached this settlement with Eni and Nigerian Agip Exploration Limited (NAEL), effectively ending the protracted dispute over OPL 245. Fagbemi emphasised that resolving the dispute over OPL 245 will recalibrate the national economy and bolster the federal government's fiscal position. According to him, early in the administration, President Tinubu directed that all disputes over the oil block be resolved amicably in the best interests of the Nigerian people. "The clear vision and deep commitment of President Tinubu provided the political will required to bring closure to this protracted dispute. The agreement demonstrates Nigeria’s commitment to transparency, accountability, and the rule of law." The Attorney-General explained that the settlement, which will culminate in a Consent Arbitral Award, not only resolves a complex international dispute but also restores Nigeria’s credibility as a responsible partner in global business. He further highlighted several strategic economic benefits expected from the resolution, including the removal of legal and fiscal uncertainties that previously hindered the development of the oil block. "This development will pave the way for large-scale investments, stimulate job creation, and reinforce Nigeria’s position as a leading energy producer in Africa," he said. Fagbemi also noted that projected revenues from the asset could now be included in the country’s medium-term fiscal framework, thereby supporting budget stability, long-term economic planning, and debt sustainability. He added that resolving the dispute through negotiated settlement rather than prolonged arbitration underscores Nigeria’s commitment to alternative dispute resolution and enhances the country’s credibility in international commercial and arbitration circles. “This settlement sends a clear signal to the global community that Nigeria is open for business and committed to fairness and respect for contractual obligations,” he said. The Attorney-General also commended key institutions and stakeholders that contributed to the successful resolution, including the Ministry of Petroleum Resources, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, and international partners such as Eni and Shell. He emphasised that the settlement represents the triumph of dialogue over conflict and national interest over narrow considerations. “With this agreement, Nigeria can now move forward with confidence, ensuring that the development of OPL 245 becomes a source of prosperity for the nation and future generations,” Fagbemi stated. In view of the extraordinary economic challenges arising from the ongoing conflict in the region, I have decided to take extraordinary measures to protect the public and manage resources responsibly. Until the petroleum crisis is resolved, official fuel supply for provincial ministers will be suspended. I have also ordered an immediate 50% reduction in petrol and diesel allowances for government officers vehicles. The protocol vehicles accompanying provincial ministers and senior government officials have also been restricted. Only one vehicle will be allowed for essential security purposes. Government offices will implement a work-from-home policy, with only essential staff attending offices. Schools, colleges, and universities will remain closed from 10 March to 31 March, while examinations will continue as scheduled. Educational institutions may conduct online classes during this period. For the convenience of citizens, e-business services and “Maryam Ki Dastak” services will continue. Official matters will be handled through online meetings and teleconferences. All government outdoor events have been suspended, including the Horse and Cattle Show cultural festival, which has been postponed. To ensure strict oversight of petroleum supplies, District Petroleum Monitoring Committees have been established in every district. The Punjab Information Technology Board (PITB) has been tasked with developing a Track and Trace system for petroleum products, with participation from district administration, police, and other relevant departments. Under the work-from-home policy, only additional support staff movement will be restricted; government work will continue without interruption. The private sector is advised to adopt work-from-home arrangements where possible, avoid unnecessary events, and limit on-site staff to essential personnel. District administrations have been directed to strictly monitor transport fares and take strong legal action against overcharging. The supply and prices of essential food items will also be closely monitored across Punjab. I urge the public to avoid outdoor functions, late-night shopping, and unnecessary hoarding of essential goods during this challenging period. I also pay tribute to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir for their courageous leadership and decisive actions during this difficult crisis. Brave nations confront difficult times with unity, patience, and wisdom and the people of Pakistan will do the same.

Thematic Sessions of the Regional Best Practices Seminar (South) under Aspirational Districts and Blocks Programme at NITI Aayog The Regional Best Practices Seminar (South) under the Aspirational Districts and Blocks Programme (ADP/ABP) was held in Vishakhapatnam, bringing together District Collectors, state officials and development practitioners from across southern India. The seminar featured three thematic technical sessions highlighting district-led interventions in Education and Skill Development; Health, Nutrition and Social Development; and Skill Development across Aspirational Districts and Blocks. Technical Session I on Education and Skill Development showcased innovative initiatives including the NIRMAN initiative from Alluri Sitarama Raju district, aimed at improving foundational learning outcomes, and the Rural Incubation Centre model from NTR district, which promotes innovation and entrepreneurship among rural youth. Technical Sessions II and III on Health, Nutrition and Skill Development highlighted impactful best practices such as the Anaemia Mukt initiative from Bidar district, addressing anaemia among women and children, and the Amma Rakshitha programme from Nirmal district, focused on improving maternal health outcomes. Additional innovative practices were also shared by the District Collector of Kurnool district, showcasing district-led approaches to strengthen youth skill development. In his concluding remarks, Shri Rohit Kumar, Additional Secretary & Mission Director – ADP/ABP, NITI Aayog, emphasised the importance of documenting and scaling best practices and encouraged districts to build on successful models while fostering cross-learning. The seminar concluded with key learnings and actionable insights, reaffirming the importance of peer learning and knowledge-sharing platforms in strengthening district-led innovation and accelerating transformation in India’s most underserved regions. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #AspirationalDistricts #AspirationalBlocks #BestPractices #ADP #ABP #DistrictTransformation #DataDrivenGovernance #LastMileDelivery #TransformingIndia

Women’s rights are never permanently guaranteed. They are won through constant struggle, through courage, and through vigilance that must never weaken. On March 8, as on every other day of the year. A tribute to all the women who, every day, keep this fight alive. Those who commit themselves, who take action, who raise their voices when necessary, and who, through their courage and dedication, inspire present and future generations. Today, my thoughts are especially with the women living through the wars and conflicts affecting our world. As the first victims of violence, they are also, everywhere, essential actors in peace, resistance and reconstruction. While some seek to destroy, they rebuild. While some seek to subjugate, they stand firm. France stands by their side, tirelessly and without rest. I extend a message of solidarity and admiration to the women of Iran. Their courage commands respect and reminds the world that freedom can never be silenced. The fight for women’s rights is a universal one. It is the fight of both women and men, and it concerns us all. It will go on. For as long as equality is not a reality everywhere, France will be there to take action.

11 countries have sent Ukraine requests for help in intercepting and shooting down Iranian "suicide drones." Among them are the US, European countries, and Iran's neighbors, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said during a meeting of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief's Staff. Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) I held a Staff meeting. Our primary focus was the destabilization caused by the war in Iran and the corresponding risks for global markets, the countries of the region, and Ukraine’s closest partners who support us in defending against Russian aggression. The issue is complex – all these developments in the Middle East and the Gulf region directly affect Europe, and Ukraine in particular, as well as other parts of the world, including critically important supplies to Ukraine and the security and well-being of our people. Reports were delivered by the Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council, the heads of intelligence agencies, the Security Service of Ukraine, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Minister of Defense. We analyzed the main prospects of this war in Iran and the possible consequences if it drags on. We also reviewed in detail requests from states for security support from our side in countering “shahed” drones and other similar challenges. As of now, there are 11 requests from countries neighboring Iran, European states, and the U.S. There is clear interest in Ukraine’s experience in protecting lives, relevant interceptors, electronic warfare systems, and training. Ukraine is ready to respond positively to requests from those who help us protect the lives of Ukrainians and the independence of Ukraine. Some requests have already been met with concrete decisions and specific support. The National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine, together with the General Staff and the Defense Forces, will determine which additional requests our state can respond to positively, without reducing our own ability to defend ourselves. Ukraine’s priority is clear: the Iranian regime must not gain any advantage over those defending lives. And everyone must work together for tangible stabilization both in the region and in global markets. Ukraine has long proposed that partners upgrade and strengthen joint capabilities to protect lives. We have spoken about joint defense against drones and missiles, as well as about destroying the relevant production facilities of aggressor regimes – weapons production used in attacks, including those happening now. Each of these regimes has set itself against the world – and this requires a response. Every “shahed” production site is known. The Iranian and Russian regimes support one another, and more information is emerging, including about Russian components in “shaheds” striking Iran’s neighbors. The world is certainly stronger than anyone trying to destabilize it. We expect our partners to act with sufficient determination. The SMILE satellite has arrived in Kourou, French Guiana entering its final countdown for a launch this spring 🚀. SMILE stands for Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer. Why does this matter? While the Northern Lights are breathtaking, the solar winds that cause them can trigger geomagnetic storms that impact our daily lives, such as affecting navigation systems. SMILE will give us our first-ever global look at how Earth’s magnetic shield protects us from these solar storms. Airbus innovation at work: Airbus in Spain led the development of the payload, including four high-tech instruments designed to photograph the "invisible" and measure the energy of the Sun. Get ready to see the Earth’s defence system like never before! 🔭

Провів Ставку. Передусім про дестабілізацію через війну в Ірані та відповідні ризики для глобальних ринків, країн регіону та найближчих партнерів України, які підтримують нас у захисті від російської агресії. Проблематика комплексна: усі ці події на Близькому Сході та в регіоні Затоки прямо впливають на Європу – і, зокрема, на Україну, – на інші частини світу, на критично важливе постачання в Україну, безпеку й добробут наших людей. Були доповіді секретаря РНБО, керівників розвідок, СБУ, МЗС України, міністра оборони. Проаналізували основні перспективи цієї війни в Ірані та можливі наслідки її затягування. Детально розглянули й запити держав на безпекову підтримку з нашого боку – в протидії «шахедам» та іншим подібним викликам. Станом на цей час є 11 запитів від країн – сусідів Ірану, європейських держав та Америки. Чітка зацікавленість в українському досвіді захисту життя, відповідних перехоплювачах, системах РЕБ, тренуванні. Україна готова реагувати позитивно на запити тих, хто допомагає нам самим захищати життя українців та незалежність України. На частину запитів ми вже відповіли конкретними рішеннями, конкретною підтримкою. РНБО України разом з Генеральним штабом та Силами оборони визначатимуть, на які ще запити до нашої держави ми можемо відреагувати позитивно – так, щоб не знижувати наші власні можливості захищатись. Пріоритет України чіткий: іранський режим не повинен отримати жодної переваги над захисниками життя, і треба працювати всім разом для відчутної стабілізації як у регіоні, так і на глобальних ринках. Україна давно пропонує партнерам оновити та посилити спільні можливості захищати життя. Ми говорили і про спільний захист від дронів та ракет, і про знищення відповідних виробництв режимів-агресорів – виробництв зброї, яка використовується в тому числі зараз в ударах. Кожен з таких режимів сам протиставив себе світу, і потрібні відповіді на це. Кожна точка виробництва «шахедів» відома. Іранський та російський режими підтримують один одного, і все більше інформації, зокрема, про російські деталі в «шахедах», які бʼють по сусідах Ірану. Світ точно сильніший, ніж будь-хто, хто намагається його дестабілізувати. Розраховуємо, що партнери будуть достатньо рішучими. Дякую всім, хто допомагає!

I held a Staff meeting. Our primary focus was the destabilization caused by the war in Iran and the corresponding risks for global markets, the countries of the region, and Ukraine’s closest partners who support us in defending against Russian aggression. The issue is complex – all these developments in the Middle East and the Gulf region directly affect Europe, and Ukraine in particular, as well as other parts of the world, including critically important supplies to Ukraine and the security and well-being of our people. Reports were delivered by the Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council, the heads of intelligence agencies, the Security Service of Ukraine, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Minister of Defense. We analyzed the main prospects of this war in Iran and the possible consequences if it drags on. We also reviewed in detail requests from states for security support from our side in countering “shahed” drones and other similar challenges. As of now, there are 11 requests from countries neighboring Iran, European states, and the U.S. There is clear interest in Ukraine’s experience in protecting lives, relevant interceptors, electronic warfare systems, and training. Ukraine is ready to respond positively to requests from those who help us protect the lives of Ukrainians and the independence of Ukraine. Some requests have already been met with concrete decisions and specific support. The National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine, together with the General Staff and the Defense Forces, will determine which additional requests our state can respond to positively, without reducing our own ability to defend ourselves. Ukraine’s priority is clear: the Iranian regime must not gain any advantage over those defending lives. And everyone must work together for tangible stabilization both in the region and in global markets. Ukraine has long proposed that partners upgrade and strengthen joint capabilities to protect lives. We have spoken about joint defense against drones and missiles, as well as about destroying the relevant production facilities of aggressor regimes – weapons production used in attacks, including those happening now. Each of these regimes has set itself against the world – and this requires a response. Every “shahed” production site is known. The Iranian and Russian regimes support one another, and more information is emerging, including about Russian components in “shaheds” striking Iran’s neighbors. The world is certainly stronger than anyone trying to destabilize it. We expect our partners to act with sufficient determination. Thank you to everyone who helps!

During ransomware or APT incident response, organisations are often already at their limits Admins work nights and weekends. Incident responders try to identify compromised systems and plan remediation. Adding large-scale compromise assessments across thousands of endpoints is often simply too much operational overhead. That’s why scanning backups can be such a powerful control point. Before systems are restored, restore points can be scanned for the things that really matter in remediation scenarios: webshells, backdoors, reverse shells, malicious scripts, hack tools or tunnelling utilities that attackers may have left behind This works even where EDR visibility does not help - because the relevant data sits at rest inside backup images. Traditional AV engines can contribute here, but they mainly focus on known malware and binary verdicts. THOR looks at a very different problem space: attacker tooling, persistence mechanisms, obfuscation techniques and suspicious traces that often show up in real intrusions. When I worked as a security consultant, and even today, my recommendation for backup validation before restore would be simple: scan the backups once with an AV engine and once with THOR. The coverage you get from that combination is, in my view, far more valuable than throwing dozens of AV engines at the same backup set - because AV and THOR are not looking for the same things. Вскоре он погиб в заключении России. 19 декабря 2025 года представитель общественного движения «Свободная Черкесия» Беслан Кмузов рассказал (facebook.com/bkmuzov/posts/p…) о произошедшей за месяц до этого смерти 59-летнего Заура Шогенцукова, внука известного черкесского культурного деятеля Али Шогенцукова. По данным Кмузова, с которым поговорила «Сота», в августе 2024 года Шогенцуков прилетел в Минск и оттуда попал в Украину, перейдя пограничную реку Припять. После этого он сдался пограничникам и начал проходить проверку СБУ, в ходе ожидания решения которой, по данным Кмузова, ссылавшегося на сообщения самого Шогенцукова, «его избивали, требуя признания в том, что он является засланным агентом», и готовили к обмену, что закончилось вскрытием Шогенцуковым вен. В итоге задержанного отправили в СИЗО за незаконное пересечение границы и приговорили к заключению. После того, как Шогенцуков смог связаться с черкесской общественностью в эмиграции, к ситуации было привлечено внимание украинских военных: обмен Шогенцукова был отменен, дело отправлено на пересмотр, а с февраля 2025 года представитель «Кавказского легиона» ВСУ Ладо Гамсахурдия через суд добивался (t.me/georgia_man/5484) перевода Шогенцукова в его подразделение. Решение об отказе было вынесено в октябре, а 27 ноября 2025 года Шогенцуков из миграционной тюрьмы (Черниговский ПТПИ) был передан в Управление миграционной службы по региону, считая, согласно его звонку родственникам, что теперь его заберут в ВСУ. Однако в действительности Шогенцукова депортировали, а 19 декабря, как стало известно Кмузову, уже в российском Нальчике тело Шогенцукова было выдано родственникам. 24 января 2026 года ситуацию по просьбе «Соты» прокомментировал (facebook.com/bkmuzov/posts/p…) «Легион «Свобода России» (ЛСР), в который Шогенцуков стремился попасть. По данным ЛСР, он «никогда не находился в нашем подчинении». При этом в ЛСР подтвердили проходившую в отношении Шогенцукова проверку: «…положительного решения от СБУ на освобождение Заура и направление его для прохождения службы в ЛСР принято не было». Также ЛСР подтвердил ключевой факт: Шогенцуков, действительно, был депортирован после 27 ноября 2025 года, однако страна депортации из сообщения осталась неизвестной: «Все последующие решения — относительно его статуса, содержания, судебных процедур и депортации (подчеркиваем: депортации, а не обмена) — принимались исключительно государственными органами Украины в рамках закона и установленной процедуры». Миграционная служба Украина в ответ на запрос «Соты» 6 марта отказалась раскрывать сведения о Шогенцукове, сославшись на тайну персональных данных, однако заявила, что «иностранцы <…> не могут быть насильственно <…> высланы <…> в государство, где их жизни или свободе угрожает опасность <…>». Российские органы власти запрос «Соты» проигнорировали. Добавим, что, по данным Кмузова, Шогенцуков в Черниговской области содержался вместе с также пытавшимся вступить в ВСУ Алексеем Герасимовым, в мае 2025 года, согласно статье (verstka.media/istoriya-zhite…) «Верстки», выданным в РФ в рамках обмена и арестованным по делу о терроризме. The establishment of the National Infrastructure Fund is the most consequential initiative in the development history of our nation. The fund marks a new chapter in financing our transformation, making us the architects of our own future. It will close the infrastructure financing gap by raising over KSh5 trillion to fund key projects, including the production of 10,000 megawatts of clean energy, 50 mega dams, 200 micro-dams and more than 1,000 small dams, 2,500km of dual carriageways, and 28,000km of roads. Additionally, we will have the necessary financing for extending the Standard Gauge Railway from Naivasha to Malaba and Kisumu and expanding Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, among many others. The fund will help us structure our priorities, and package them into investable instruments. It will also de-risk our economy by providing a framework that attracts investors rather than merely encourage them to invest. The Kenyan National Infrastructure Fund is not an experiment; it is a model that has succeeded in other jurisdictions. With it, our journey to attaining first-world economy status is within reach. Glad that today, we have delivered a pledge we made to the people of Kenya in our manifesto. Pakistan's defense strategy and infrastructure are shaped by its unique geopolitical realities, primarily immediate border threats and the need for rapid, high-intensity responses, unlike the long-duration, expeditionary role of major U.S. forward bases. 1. Proximity of Threats Pakistan faces active border adversaries with significant conventional and non conventional capabilities. This demands quick-reaction forces and dispersed, survivable assets rather than centralized mega-bases. 2. Doctrine of Rapid Offensive/Defensive Action Pakistan's warfighting concept emphasizes swift, decisive operations often aiming to neutralize or degrade enemy capabilities within hours in the event of full scale conflict. This contrasts with U.S. bases, which support prolonged campaigns against opponents with limited or no meaningful air power. 3. Design Philosophy of U.S. Bases vs. Pakistani Airfields Facilities like Al Udeid are built for sustained, long-term operations in relatively permissive environments against non-peer adversaries. They serve as secure hubs for command, logistics, and large scale airpower projection over extended periods. 4. Use of National Motorways as Dispersed Runways Pakistan has strategically designed sections of its motorways to function as emergency or alternate runways. This allows fighter aircraft to operate from hidden, distributed locations, enhancing survivability and operational flexibility if primary airbases are targeted or degraded. 5. Vulnerability of Fixed Bases in High Intensity War In a full scale conventional conflict, large, fixed installations become high-value "centers of gravity" and potential sitting ducks for precision missile barrages or saturation attacks. Pakistan mitigates this through dispersal, mobility, rapid counterstrikes, and layered defenses approaches less feasible for massive, static overseas U.S. bases reliant on host nation protection and layered theater defenses. In short, while Al Udeid's sheer size and hardening make it resilient to piecemeal attacks, Pakistan's setup prioritizes speed, dispersion, and offensive initiative to offset numerical or infrastructural asymmetries. Inspired by Commonwealth Poet Laureate Selina Tusitala Marsh, we invite you to respond to a single prompt: ‘Thread’. Dancers thread movement between bodies. Musicians thread melody through rhythm. Painters thread colour. Storytellers thread narrative. Photographers thread light. What thread do you bring to the Commonwealth? We welcome submissions across visual, literary and performing arts, including painting, photography, poetry, music, dance, spoken word and short film. Both artists and non-artists can participate. You can submit as an individual or a group. All eligible submissions will be displayed in the virtual Commonwealth Quilt. Up to three submissions per region will be selected for a physical exhibition during the Commonwealth People’s Forum and will receive a £200 award. NITI Aayog Convenes Regional Best Practices Seminar (South) under Aspirational District and Block Programme! The Regional Best Practices Seminar (South) under the Aspirational Districts and Blocks Programme (ADP/ABP) was conducted today at Visakhapatnam, bringing together District Collectors, State officials and development practitioners from across southern states to showcase innovative governance practices and accelerate district transformation. Shri Rohit Kumar, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, ADP/ABP, NITI Aayog, in his keynote address provided an overview of the Aspirational Districts and Blocks Programme and appreciated the sustained efforts of District administrations, Block officials and frontline functionaries in driving development outcomes on the ground. He emphasised that the programme should evolve into a Jan Andolan, with strong community participation and convergence across departments. He also noted that a majority of the programme indicators are nearing saturation in several districts and appreciated the strong performance of southern states under the ADP/ABP framework. Delivering the Special Address, Shri Anant Shankar, Joint Secretary, Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, highlighted the State’s focus on removing absolute poverty through targeted initiatives including the Zero Poverty Mission, guided by the vision of P4 – Public, Private, People Partnerships. He also noted the steady progress made by Andhra Pradesh and other southern states across key development indicators under the programme. The event also witnessed the unveiling of the Best Practices Compendium, showcasing impactful initiatives from districts across southern India that are improving outcomes in Education, Healthcare, Nutrition and Livelihoods. District Collectors and senior officers from Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands presented innovative district-level initiatives and participated in discussions on scaling best practices, strengthening convergence and improving last-mile service delivery. The establishment of the National Infrastructure Fund is the most consequential initiative in the development history of our nation. The fund marks a new chapter in financing our transformation, making us the architects of our own future. It will close the infrastructure financing gap by raising over KSh5 trillion to fund key projects, including the production of 10,000 megawatts of clean energy, 50 mega dams, 200 micro-dams and more than 1,000 small dams, 2,500km of dual carriageways, and 28,000km of roads. Additionally, we will have the necessary financing for extending the Standard Gauge Railway from Naivasha to Malaba and Kisumu and expanding Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, among many others. The fund will help us structure our priorities, and package them into investable instruments. It will also de-risk our economy by providing a framework that attracts investors rather than merely encourage them to invest. The Kenyan National Infrastructure Fund is not an experiment; it is a model that has succeeded in other jurisdictions. With it, our journey to attaining first-world economy status is within reach. Glad that today, we have delivered a pledge we made to the people of Kenya in our manifesto. Assented to the National Infrastructure Fund Bill, State House, Nairobi, in the presence of captains of industry from Kenya, Africa and the world.

Let’s look at how President Dr Arif Alvi (@ArifAlvi) ran the Presidency during the austerity drive. When Pakistan faced severe economic pressure, Imran Khan’s government directed all state institutions to cut costs. This wasn’t just lip service. The austerity drive was actually implemented — not followed by buying fleets of luxury vehicles or Gulfstream jets while preaching restraint. The Presidency followed through. The President House budget was reduced by ~50%, falling from about Rs 963M in earlier years to Rs 507M in FY2020-21. Marco Silva is three short of a century of wins as Fulham head coach. He’s overseen 220 games in almost five years in charge. Only Pep Guardiola and Mikel Arteta have been in charge of their clubs longer in the Premier League atm. Silva's highly regarded, rightly so, as he regularly over-achieves with the playing cards he’s dealt: got Fulham up as champions in first season (21/22), then 10th, 13th, 11th and currently 10th in the Premier League. Safe hands, guaranteed PL security, club boards like that. But Silva's approach to the FA Cup tie against Southampton felt a mistake, a missed opportunity, wasting a chance for Fulham fans to enjoy some added adrenalin to another safe season, some quickened step in their Spring. Fans understandably want a run at a Cup, especially as Fulham aren’t at risk of relegation (12 points above drop zone). Maybe Silva’s remit is to finish in the European places. Fulham are only four points off seventh. Maybe. The FA Cup also offers a route into Europe. Did Silva underestimate Championship visitors? Saints were in good form, unbeaten in 9 going into the game, inspired by Eckart and shouldn’t have been taken lightly. Silva resting the likes of Sander Berge was understandable, given the midfielder’s workload. It was not the fact that Silva made 9 changes - Wilson was injured, there was still plenty of talent on show - but that he didn’t make more changes earlier in a game scoreless until the 91st minute. Iwobi for Cairney after 65 minutes was the only change until 89 when King replaced Smith Rowe. Why not King earlier? Silva pointed to chances not taken – Fulham had 24 attempts on goal. Why not Raul Jimenez earlier? Fulham’s second top scorer (after Wilson) arrived at 92 for Reed – after Stewart had scored for Southampton (91). Added time stretched to 99 mins. Silva used only three subs. Saints march on. Fulham reflect on a missed opportunity. If Silva is leaving this summer, he could have left fans with the great memory of a Cup run. #FFC

1. #CutTheClutter shifts its gaze from the Middle East to the East, as China sets its economic growth target at 4.5-5%, the lowest since 1991. That’s a big shift for an economy that has averaged double-digit growth for years. In this episode, we look at the factors behind China’s move, explain what’s next & the shift in country’s priorities. 2. Since 1985-86, China’s growth has generally stayed above 10%. In some years, like 1993 & 2008, growth even crossed 14%. That’s how China suddenly left India behind & the gap kept widening. Now, this shouldn’t be cause for celebration. Because China, India, US, Europe are major economies & what happens to them affects the world. 3. China’s target is to become a middle-income developed economy by 2035. Its per capita income in 2026, according to IMF, will be upwards of $14,000. The World Bank definition for a developed country is $20,000 per capita income. Trouble is, China now faces the middle-income trap — a demographic trap of developed nations before quite becoming one. 4. China is aging fast: 23% of its population is already above 60. Its average age is 40.6 years &, by 2040, that could touch 48. China is getting old very rapidly & that is what is inviting the country into the middle-income trap because this population is not growing. Last year, the population declined by 40 lakh. 5. China’s big priority now is to increase consumption, & they need what countries like ours are trying to fight — inflation. China’s had negative inflation for the past many years. Can they turn the tide now? Looks tough because almost everything has become cheaper — from housing to food —indicating weak domestic demand. 6. It’s basically really tiny radar, which also took off during WW2. NLJDs allow you to detect even a single transistor hidden inside something. Even if unpowered! There’s a story from the 80’s where the USSR sprinkled tons of loose diodes into the concrete mixture when building the US embassy. This worked like radar chaff, making it seem like there were thousands of bugs in the entire building, which would hide any real bugs.

Investing in rural women is a trillion-dollar opportunity. Women are central to rural economies - as farmers, entrepreneurs and leaders. Yet they continue to face significant structural barriers to land, finance and markets. Women make up 41% of the global agrifood workforce, contributing across the entire value chain from production to processing and marketing. Yet less than 15% of global landholders are women, limiting their ability to fully participate in and benefit from rural economic growth. Closing these gaps is not only a matter of equality, but also a powerful economic opportunity. Evidence shows that investing in rural women could raise incomes for 58 million people and strengthen resilience for 235 million more. At @IFAD, we invest where impact is greatest: at the #FirstMile of food systems. By expanding access to finance, technology, knowledge and markets, we are helping rural women strengthen livelihoods, build businesses and drive transformation across rural economies. On #InternationalWomensDay, the message is clear: investing in rural women strengthens food systems, economies and global resilience. Learn more: Rural women, from investment to impact #IWD2026 #YearOfTheWomanFarmer

CC: @Shayan86 @AuroraIntel @Osinttechnical @sentdefender @War_Mapper @tom_bike @Arabosint @talhagin @AMK_Mapping_ @AnalyticaCamil1 🫡 Soar (@SoarAtlas) As conflicts break out, AI-generated fake imagery is becoming more common online. At Soar Atlas, we manually review every satellite image and map that comes through our system to ensure uploads remain trustworthy. One image currently circulating shows an air base with planes painted on the ground. While it may look convincing at first glance, there are a few clues that suggest it isn’t real satellite imagery. First, most commercial satellites, such as those operated by Maxar Technologies or Planet Labs, capture imagery at roughly 30cm per pixel. Because of this physical limitation, extremely fine details usually aren’t visible from space. If an image appears unusually sharp or shows very small features with perfect clarity, it’s worth questioning. Satellites don’t capture imagery the way it’s often portrayed in movies. They aren’t constantly watching every location with a live camera in the sky. Most Earth-observation satellites travel in fixed orbits and only pass over the same area at certain times, which means many major events are not captured immediately and may only be imaged hours or even days later depending on when the next pass occurs. Weather is another major limitation. Cloud cover frequently blocks optical satellite imagery, making it difficult to capture clear views of the ground. While some satellites use radar to see through clouds, these systems produce radar imagery rather than traditional photograph looking imagery, which can be harder for the public to interpret visually. It’s also important to look for a source. Authentic satellite imagery is almost always credited to the provider, often through a watermark or attribution. If there’s no source attached, that’s a warning sign. Another useful check is whether the imagery is georeferenced. When imagery is properly placed over real-world maps, such as those on Soar Atlas, it becomes much easier to verify whether features actually line up with the surrounding environment. AI will often get these kinds of details wrong. Finally, keep an eye out for AI tool marks or watermarks, such as the small star symbol added by Gemini in the corner. Every image on soaratlas.com we've verified. If you think something doesn't look right, click the three dots and report the map or ping us! As AI tools improve, spotting fakes will become harder. During this conflict we’ve unfortunately come across many examples, so it’s important to stay cautious and take a moment to question images before sharing them. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/SoarAtlas/status/2030896263567433888#m

रेलवे में बड़े बदलाव की तैयारी, बदलेगी 10 साल पुरानी PPP पॉलिसी; क्‍या होगा फायदा? भारतीय रेलवे की तरफ से लगातार यात्री सुव‍िधाओं पर फोकस क‍िया जा रहा है. अब भारतीय रेलवे ने अपनी 10 साल से ज्यादा पुरानी प्राइवेट पार्टनरशिप पॉल‍िसी (PPP) में बदलाव करने का प्‍लान क‍िया है. इसके तहत रेलवे की तरफ से दो बड़े बदलाव का प्रपोजल द‍िया गया है. इन बदलाव से प्राइवेट निवेशकों को ज्यादा स‍िक्‍योर‍िटी म‍िल सकेगी, रिस्क कम होगा और रेलवे प्रोजेक्ट तेजी से पूरे होंगे. अब प्राइवेट कंपनियां पहले से ज्‍यादा आत्‍मव‍िश्‍वास के साथ रेलवे में इनवेस्‍ट कर सकेंगी. मौजूदा पीपीपी (PPP) प्रोजेक्ट में कंसेशन पीरियड 20 से 35 साल तक का होता है. रेलवे की तरफ से इसे बढ़ाकर 50 साल करने का प्रस्ताव द‍िया गया है. इससे प्राइवेट पार्टनर को अपना इनवेस्‍टमेंट आसानी से रिकवर करने के ल‍िए ज्यादा समय मिलेगा और प्रोजेक्ट ज्यादा आकर्षक बनेंगे. रेलवे म‍िन‍िस्‍टर अश्‍व‍िनी वैष्णव की तरफ से हाल ही में गत‍ि शक्ति मल्टी-मॉडल कार्गो टर्मिनल्स (GCT) के लिए 50 साल के कंसेशन पीर‍ियड की घोषणा की गई, यही नई पॉलिसी की शुरुआत है. . . अभी पीपीपी (PPP) प्रोजेक्ट्स में जमीन अधिग्रहण का खर्च और प्रोसेस प्राइवेट प्लेयर को देना होता है, जबकि जमीन रेलवे लेता है. इस कारण अक्सर देरी होती है. लेक‍िन अब प्रस्‍ताव‍ित बदलाव के तहत रेलवे की तरफ से खर्च और प्रोसेस को लेकर पूरी जिम्मेदारी ली जाएगी. हाइवे प्रोजेक्ट के अनुभव के आधार पर यह कदम उठाया जा रहा है. इससे प्रोजेक्‍ट में देरी नहीं होगी और वे समय से पूरे हो सकेंगे. रेलवे की तरफ से मार्च 2028 तक पीपीपी मॉडल के तहत 15 प्रोजेक्ट का चुनाव क‍िया गया है. इनकी कुल लागत 35,817 करोड़ रुपये है. इनमें नई लाइन बिछाना, ट्रैक को डबल करना और स्टेशन रीडेवलपमेंट शामिल है. कुछ प्रोजेक्ट फाइनल अप्रूवल के लिए भेजे गए हैं. 2012 की मौजूदा पीपीपी पॉलिसी के तहत दिसंबर 2025 तक महज 18 प्रोजेक्ट्स (16,686 करोड़ रुपये) पूरे हुए हैं. 16,362 करोड़ रुपये की लागत वाले 7 प्रोजेक्ट पर काम चल रहा है. नई पॉलिसी से PPP में तेजी आएगी और रेलवे इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर मजबूत होगा. #IndianRailways #Rules #RailwayRules #IndianRailwaysPolicy #PrivatePartnershipPolicy

Cheetah numbers in India reach 53, as Jwala gives birth to 5 cubs at Kuno; Indian-born cubs rise to 33 10th successful Cheetah litter on Indian soil, reflecting dedicated efforts, skill & commitment of veterinarians, field staff: Shri @byadavbjp 📝 pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.…

Cheetahs cross half-century 🐆 A moment of great pride for Project Cheetah as Jwala, the Namibian Cheetah and a successful third-time mother, gave birth to five cubs today at the Kuno National Park. With this birth, the number of Indian-born thriving cubs has risen to 33, marking the 10th successful cheetah litter on Indian soil—another important milestone in India’s cheetah conservation journey. This achievement reflects the dedicated efforts, skill, and commitment of the veterinarians, field staff and all involved who continue to work tirelessly on the ground. With the arrival of these cubs, the total cheetah population in India has now reached 53. A historic and heart-warming moment for wildlife conservation. May Jwala and her cubs grow strong and race ahead, carrying India’s cheetah story to even greater heights.

The publication was issued as part of the Varuna Alert series on 9 March 2026. Compiled by Rashmi Yadav, the report provides a curated overview of significant maritime news and analytical insights sourced from national and international platforms. According to NMF, the edition highlights major developments in maritime security, including emerging threats, naval strategies, and regional stability issues. It also examines updates related to maritime forces, focusing on naval operations, exercises, and force modernisation initiatives across various regions. The publication further explores key aspects of the global shipping industry, ports, and the ocean economy, providing perspectives on trade dynamics, port infrastructure, and evolving developments shaping the maritime sector. Environmental concerns remain another central theme in the report, with discussions on climate change, marine conservation, and sustainable maritime practices. The analysis also delves into the geopolitical dimension of maritime affairs, assessing strategic shifts and intensifying global maritime competition. NMF clarified that the compilation draws from original sources and undergoes minor editorial refinement by subject-matter experts to enhance clarity and context. For months, we have consistently raised serious concerns with @ECISVEEP regarding SIR in Bengal. Repeated representations, documented irregularities, and unanswered questions ultimately forced us to approach the Supreme Court, a step that should never have been necessary in a democracy. The evidence is alarming. Almost 63.6 lakh voters have been deleted, while only 42,251 Form-7 objections were filed yet 5.46 lakh deletions executed. At the same time, 6.33 lakh Form-6 applications resulted in barely 1.82 lakh additions. Over 60 lakh voters remain under adjudication. Statutory authority of EROs has been bypassed, Micro-Observers given veto power, valid government documents rejected, and even critical instructions reportedly issued informally. When the process of revising the voter roll becomes opaque and arbitrary, the very foundation of electoral democracy is at stake. The Election Commission must act decisively to restore transparency, legality, and protect every citizen’s right to vote.

We have written to the ECI flagging serious irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls in Bengal. Over 63 lakh voters have been deleted, while more than 60 lakh cases remain under adjudication, raising alarming questions about transparency and due process. Even more troubling, only about 42,251 Form-7 objections were filed, yet over 5.4 lakh voters have been deleted, exposing a shocking mismatch that demands immediate explanation. Such large-scale deletions, procedural deviations, and opaque processes threaten the very integrity of the electoral system. Democracy cannot survive if eligible voters are arbitrarily removed from the rolls. The ECI must urgently address these violations and ensure that every citizen’s constitutional right to vote is protected. Video

Mojtaba Khamenei - Supreme leader of Iran: Mojtaba Khamenei may represent a more hardline and upgraded version of his father. Although he has never held a formal position, he has long operated behind the scenes in his father’s office and is widely seen as one of the most powerful figures in the Supreme Leader’s inner circle. His rise has been strongly supported by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), and there is little doubt that their influence would grow further under his leadership. At the same time, given his limited experience in security and foreign policy, more seasoned figures such as Ali Larijani and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf may play important roles in shaping decision-making around him. Ironically, the elimination of Khamenei may have paved the way for the son’s rise. A new leader entering office under such circumstances could be deeply motivated by a desire to retaliate against Israel and the United States. Iran’s future under Mojtaba could therefore become more rigid. Domestically, political openness is unlikely. Internationally, Iran may pursue a more dogmatic foreign policy while deepening its strategic alignment with Russia and China. Contrary to what some in Washington might hope, Mojtaba Khamenei would likely be among the last Iranian leaders inclined to engage with the United States. His appointment could prolong confrontation with Iran, as compromise may be difficult to achieve. At the same time, it remains unclear how much formal authority he would ultimately wield. Even if his personal authority is more limited than his father’s, the IRGC is likely to become even more dominant in shaping Iran’s strategic direction. Some may believe that such a succession could accelerate protests inside Iran. That outcome cannot be ruled out—but it would be a mistake to underestimate both the power of the IRGC and its determination to secure Mojtaba’s leadership. Bottom line, if Mojtaba consolidates power, Iran may adopt more hardline positions than under his father, strengthen its conventional military capabilities, deepen ties with China and Russia, and potentially reassess its nuclear strategy. At the same time, some caution is warranted. Leaders sometimes change once in power. Still, Mojtaba Khamenei does not appear likely to be the figure who introduces flexibility internally and domestically. Some may ultimately ask a difficult question: if the son’s rise leads to a more hardline Iran, should the strategic consequences of eliminating the father have been weighed more carefully in advance? #iranis Danny (Dennis) Citrinowicz ,داني سيترينوفيتش (@citrinowicz) מיהו מג'תבא ח'אמנאי? א. מג׳תבא ח׳אמנהאי עשוי להוות גרסה קיצונית ומוקצנת יותר של אביו. אמנם הוא לא נשא עד כה משרה רשמית, אך במשך שנים פעל מאחורי הקלעים בלשכתו של אביו ונחשב לאחת הדמויות החזקות בסביבתו. ב. מינויו נדחף במידה רבה על ידי משמרות המהפכה, ואין ספק כי תחת הנהגתו מעמדם רק יתחזק. עם זאת, סביר להניח שבשל חוסר ניסיונו בתחומים הביטחוניים והמדיניים, דמויות מנוסות יותר כמו עלי לאריג׳אני ומחמד באקר קאליבאף ילוו אותו מקרוב ויהיו דומיננטיים בתהליך קבלת ההחלטות. ג. ייתכן שבאופן פרדוקסלי, דווקא חיסולו של ח׳אמנהאי הוביל בפועל לעלייתו של הבן. מנהיג חדש שנכנס לתפקיד כשהוא חדור מוטיבציה לנקום בישראל ובארצות הברית על חיסול אביו ועל הפגיעה במשפחתו בתחילת המערכה. ד. העתיד של איראן תחת הנהגתו של מג׳תבא עשוי להיות עגום: ספק אם הוא יאפשר פתיחות גדולה יותר בתוך איראן, וסביר יותר שיוביל מדיניות חוץ דוגמטית ונוקשה, שתעמיק את החיבור האסטרטגי עם רוסיה וסין. ה. בסופו של דבר, ובניגוד למה שנשיא ארצות הברית דונלד טראמפ עשוי לחשוב, מג׳תבא EL OLIVO ENTRA EN LA BÓVEDA DEL FIN DEL MUNDO: ASÍ SE PROTEGE EL LEGADO GENÉTICO DEL MEDITERRÁNEO Los olivos se encuentran bajo amenaza. Entre los principales riesgos figuran el cambio climático, la pérdida acelerada de diversidad genética y la proliferación de plagas y enfermedades vinculadas a los sistemas de producción modernos, cada vez menos diversificados. La comunidad investigadora internacional considera fundamental salvaguardar el patrimonio genético de los olivos, tanto de los ejemplares silvestres como de las variedades tradicionales cultivadas, no solo por una preocupación científica, sino porque tiene repercusiones directas en la seguridad alimentaria mundial. El resguardo a largo plazo de estos recursos resulta esencial para garantizar la producción futura de aceitunas y aceite, productos característicos de la cuenca mediterránea. Así, la conservación genética del olivo se plantea como una estrategia clave ante posibles catástrofes naturales, conflictos o crisis globales que puedan afectar la disponibilidad de este cultivo. Frente a este escenario, la Bóveda Global de Semillas de Svalbard comenzó a albergar semillas de olivo. Esta bóveda constituye una de las infraestructuras más seguras para la protección de recursos fitogenéticos. Ubicada en el ártico noruego y conocida internacionalmente como la “bóveda del fin del mundo”, ofrece almacenamiento seguro y prolongado para duplicados de semillas provenientes de bancos de germoplasma de todo el mundo. Está diseñada para resistir fallos eléctricos y catástrofes, aprovechando el permafrost natural para mantener las semillas a una temperatura estable de –18 °C, considerada óptima para su conservación a largo plazo. 📲 Leé la nota completa 🔗 infob.ae/4d86sB8

آج یوم خواتین پر میں اپنی والدہ کی 1937 میں آگرہ یونیورسٹی سے حاصل کردہ بی اے کی ڈگری آپ کو پیش کر رہا ہوں—انگریزی ادب، فارسی اور اردو میں۔ وہ ہندوستان کی پہلی چار مسلمان خواتین میں شامل تھیں جنہوں نے 1937 تک بی اے کی ڈگری حاصل کی اور وہ بھی ایک ایسی دنیا میں رکاوٹیں توڑتے ہوئے جہاں اعلیٰ تعلیم کو مردوں کا میدان سمجھا جاتا تھا۔ انہوں نے ایک بار میری پڑھائی میں لاپرواہی پر نرمی سے تنبیہ کی: "عارف میاں! جو نایاب خواتین علم کی جستجو میں نکلتی تھیں، ان کے لیے گھروں میں غیر معمولی انتظامات کیے جاتے تھے۔ پردے کے لیے پردہ کھینچا جاتا تھا؛ ایک بزرگ خاتون رشتہ دار ان کے ساتھ بیٹھ کر نگرانی کرتی تھیں۔" تصور کیجیے کہ کرمانی خاندان میں کتنے بافہم مباحثے ہوئے ہوں گے تاکہ یہ ممکن ہو سکے۔ ان کی ڈگری 👇کو غور سے دیکھیں تو وہ اس دور کی کہانی خود بولے کہ صرف مردوں کے لیئے کے لیے چھاپی جاتی تھیں۔ Every ‘he’ was changed with a handwritten ‘s’ before it to make it a ‘she’. لیکن آج میرا خراج صرف میری انقلابی ماں تک محدود نہیں۔ میں پاکستان کی بانی خواتین کو خراج عقیدت پیش کرنا چاہتا ہوں—اودھ (لکھنؤ) کی بیگم حضرت محل، جنہوں نے 1857 میں انگریزوں کے خلاف جنگ کی بھرپور قیادت کی۔ اور پھر ایسی بصیرت افروز شخصیات جیسے سر سید کی والدہ بیگم عزیز النساء؛ مولانا محمد علی جوہر کی والدہ بی اماں؛ اور ناقابلِ تسخیر محترمہ فاطمہ جناح۔ کوئی بھی عقیدت کی سلامی مکمل نہیں ہو سکتی بغیر اس غیر معمولی انقلاب کے ذکر کے جو ہماری آنکھوں کے سامنے رونما ہو رہا ہے جنکا ہراول دستہ پی ٹی آئی کی خواتین ہیں۔ ان کی قربانیاں دنیا کی تاریخ میں ایک نایاب باب ہیں—ایک شعوری، اجتماعی سیاسی بیداری اور استقامت کی کہانی ہے۔ پہلی شہید میری ہی حلقے کی زہرہ شاہد حسین تھیں، جنہیں 2013 کے انتخابات کی شام کو ایم کیو ایم کے حملہ آوروں نے گولی مار کر قتل کیا —ایک بہیمانہ حرکت جو کراچی کے عوام میں مزید عزم کو بھڑکا گئی۔ اُسکے بعد ان گنت عورتوں کے پسینے، آنسوؤں اور خون سے میرے ملک کی تاریخ رقم ہو رہی ہے: قتل، وحشیانہ مار پیٹ، تشدد، من مانی گرفتاریاں، جھوٹے مقدمات اور دہایوں کی سزایں۔ ان ستاروں میں سب سے روشن میری ذاتی ہیرو دلیر ڈاکٹر یاسمین راشد ہیں—ڈاکٹر، رہنما، کینسر کی بہادر سروایئور—جن کا نہ جھکنے والا موقف ناقابلِ یقین دباؤ میں بھی وقار کی علامت ہے۔ @ImranKhanPTI کا یہ عظیم کارنامہ ہےکہ خواتین کو سیاسی قربانی میں ایسی بلندیوں تک پہنچانا جو پہلے کبھی نہ دیکھا گیا۔ جنگوں اور تنازعات میں—فلسطین، ایران سے لے کر وسیع مسلم دنیا تک—خواتین نے بے پناہ تعداد میں زیادتی، قتل اور تباہی برداشت کی ہے۔ اللہ سب کو اجر عطا فرمائے۔ مگر سیاسی طور پر، بغاوت اور وقار کی ایک دانستہ منظم تحریک کے طور پر، پی ٹی آئی کے جھنڈے تلے پاکستان کی خواتین نے تاریخ میں پہلی بارعالمی معیارِ ہمت قائم کیا ہے۔ زمانہ خود ان سنہرے لیجنڈز کی کہانیوں کو محفوظ کرے گا۔ میری ماں کو اور ہر اُس عورت کو جو قربانی کو طاقت میں بدلتی ہے: یہ یومِ خواتین آپ کا So many of us warned in explicit terms: Khamenei's "no war, no deal" is likely to result in "war followed by a terrible deal" Khamenei's systematic destruction of Iranian deterrence through his allergy to responsibility didn't help either. Danny (Dennis) Citrinowicz ,داني سيترينوفيتش (@citrinowicz) Khamenei’s strategy is what brought Iran to its current predicament. For years, he refused to move toward a bomb, believing Iran’s nuclear threshold status would be sufficient. But that assumption proved mistaken: remaining at the threshold can actually increase the likelihood of a military strike. At the same time, he was unwilling to abandon uranium enrichment in exchange for the economic relief Iran desperately needed. This strategy — no bomb, but also no real deal — has been deeply damaging for Iran. One of the first questions Iran’s leadership will likely confront after Khamenei is whether to dramatically revise this approach: either by giving up enrichment under a broad agreement, or by rushing toward a nuclear weapon — much like the strategic shift Iran made after the Iran-Iraq War. That is why the roughly 440 kg of uranium enriched to 60% stored in Isfahan matters so much. If the current regime survives, a diplomatic solution that blocks Iran’s path to a bomb may ultimately be the most responsible course. In many ways, the greatest danger of this war is that it could push Iran across the nuclear Rubicon — whether through Khamenei’s removal or through the humiliation of Iran militarily, which could drive the next leadership toward far more radical choices. #iran — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/citrinowicz/status/2030548805485998480#m

🥀March 8: Remember the Women of Iran Mahsa Amini (known as Jina) a young Iranian woman, was born on September 21, 1999 in Saqqez, Kurdistan. She was 22 years old at the time of her death. Mahsa was described as quiet yet ambitious and independent; she had recently opened a small boutique shop set up by her father and was preparing to start university studies in the fall of 2022. On September 13, 2022, while visiting Tehran with her brother, Mahsa was arrested by Iran’s Guidance Patrol (known as the morality police) for allegedly wearing her hijab “improperly” or violating compulsory hijab rules. Eyewitness accounts, family statements, and international investigations indicate she was subjected to severe physical violence and beatings inside the police van and at the detention center. She collapsed at the Vozara Detention Center, fell into a coma, and was transferred to Kasra Hospital in Tehran, where she died three days later on September 16, 2022. Mahsa Amini’s death rapidly became a national tragedy and ignited the largest wave of protests in Iran since the 1979 revolution. Her funeral in Saqqez began with chants of “Woman, Life, Freedom” (Zan, Zendegi, Azadi), which spread nationwide and turned into massive demonstrations against compulsory hijab, gender discrimination, ethnic oppression, and the Islamic Republic regime as a whole. Millions of Iranians took to the streets in what became known as the Woman, Life, Freedom movement, a symbol of women’s resistance and broader calls for freedom and equality. The protests garnered global attention and solidarity. Iranian authorities initially denied any wrongdoing, claiming Mahsa died from a pre-existing medical condition or natural causes. A 2024 United Nations Human Rights Council fact-finding mission explicitly concluded that Iran was responsible for the physical violence inflicted on Mahsa while in morality police custody, which led to her death, and described the subsequent crackdown on protesters as involving crimes against humanity, including disproportionate lethal force. This injustice is deeply rooted in the Islamic Republic’s laws, particularly the compulsory hijab mandate enforced since the 1979 revolution and codified in various articles of the Islamic Penal Code. The morality police serve as the enforcement arm of these laws, systematically targeting women with harassment, arrests, and violence. Mahsa’s case exemplified this structural oppression: a young woman lost her life simply for her appearance and choice of dress. #InternationalWomensDay #IranWar2026

On this International Women's Day, we, the women of Afghanistan, whisper our greeting from the dim corners of locked rooms, from beneath veils that have become cages, from hearts that still remember the taste of sunlight. While the world lifts lanterns of joy and crowns of triumph, we cradle silence like a bruised child. Our books gather dust in hidden graves, Our voices are ghosts forbidden to sing, We are told our laughter is sin, our learning a rebellion, our very breath in public a trespass They call it order. Let your outrage be our missing voices. Let your raised hands tear at the curtain that blinds the world. We do not ask for miracles. Only that you do not forget. On this Mother's Day, I share my mother's 1937 BA degree from Agra University—in English Literature, Persian, and Urdu. She was among the first four Muslim women in all of India who had done so by 1937, shattering barriers in a world that deemed it a male domain. She once gently chided my youthful carelessness with studies: “Arif Mian! For those rare women who dared pursue knowledge, families made extraordinary accommodations. A curtain was drawn for purdah; a senior female relative sat vigil beside her.” Imagine the quiet courage—and the family debates—that must have unfolded in the Kirmani household to make it possible. Her certificate👇whispers volumes about the era: Look closely and you will find that they were printed entirely for “he,” every instance painstakingly amended by hand with a delicate 's' inserted before “he,” transforming it into “she.” A small, defiant stroke of ink against centuries of assumption. Yet today, my tribute extends far beyond one trailblazing mother. It honors Pakistan's founding mothers—Begum Hazrat Mahal of Awadh (Lucknow), who in 1857 led fierce resistance against the British, reclaiming dignity for her people after Awadh's annexation. And visionaries like Begum Azizunnisa, mother of Sir Syed; Bi Amma, mother of Maulana Mohammad Ali Johar; the indomitable Fatima Jinnah. But no acknowledgment is complete without saluting the extraordinary revolution unfolding before our eyes: the women of PTI. Their sacrifices mark a chapter unseen in world history—a conscious, collective political awakening and endurance. The first martyr was Zahra Shahid Hussain from my own constituency, gunned down by MQM assailants on the on the eve of the 2013 elections—a brutal silencing that only ignited greater resolve. Since then, the landscape has been etched with their sweat, tears, and blood: Waves of killings, savage beatings, torture, arbitrary arrests, and fabricated sentences. Among the brightest stars is my personal hero, the fearless Dr. Yasmin Rashid—physician, leader, cancer survivor—whose unyielding stand embodies grace under unimaginable pressure. This is @ImranKhanPTI's profound legacy: Inspiring women to scale heights never before reached in political sacrifice. Across wars and conflicts—from Palestine, Iran to the broader Muslim world—women have endured rape, murder, and devastation in staggering numbers. May Allah reward them all. Yet politically, as a deliberate movement of defiance and dignity, the women of Pakistan under PTI's banner have set a global benchmark of courage as never before in history which will record these legends and their stories. To my mother and to every woman who has turned sacrifice into strength: this Mother's Day is yours.

On this Mother's Day, I share my mother's 1937 BA degree from Agra University—in English Literature, Persian, and Urdu. She was among the first four Muslim women in all of India who had done so by 1937, shattering barriers in a world that deemed it a male domain. She once gently chided my youthful carelessness with studies: “Arif Mian! For those rare women who dared pursue knowledge, families made extraordinary accommodations. A curtain was drawn for purdah; a senior female relative sat vigil beside her.” Imagine the quiet courage—and the family debates—that must have unfolded in the Kirmani household to make it possible. Her certificate👇whispers volumes about the era: Look closely and you will they were printed entirely for “he,” every instance painstakingly amended by hand with a delicate 's' inserted before “he,” transforming it into “she.” A small, defiant stroke of ink against centuries of assumption. Yet today, my tribute extends far beyond one trailblazing mother. It honors Pakistan's founding mothers—Begum Hazrat Mahal of Awadh (Lucknow), who in 1857 led fierce resistance against the British, reclaiming dignity for her people after Awadh's annexation. And visionaries like Begum Azizunnisa, mother of Sir Syed; Bi Amma, mother of Maulana Mohammad Ali Johar; the indomitable Fatima Jinnah. But no acknowledgment is complete without saluting the extraordinary revolution unfolding before our eyes: the women of PTI. Their sacrifices mark a chapter unseen in world history—a conscious, collective political awakening and endurance. The first martyr was Zahra Shahid Hussain from my own constituency, gunned down by MQM assailants on the eve of the 2013 bye-elections—a brutal silencing that only ignited greater resolve. Since then, the landscape has been etched with their sweat, tears, and blood: Waves of killings, savage beatings, torture, arbitrary arrests, and fabricated sentences. Among the brightest stars is my personal hero, the fearless Dr. Yasmin Rashid—physician, leader, cancer survivor—whose unyielding stand embodies grace under unimaginable pressure. This is @ImranKhanPTI's profound legacy: Inspiring women to scale heights never before reached in political sacrifice. Across wars and conflicts—from Palestine, Iran to the broader Muslim world—women have endured rape, murder, and devastation in staggering numbers. May Allah reward them all. Yet politically, as a deliberate movement of defiance and dignity, the women of Pakistan under PTI's banner have set a global benchmark of courage as never before in history which will record these legends and their stories. To my mother and to every woman who has turned sacrifice into strength: this Mother's Day is yours.

"We're wasting food on cattle that could feed billions of people." Gerald eats the following, in a standard week on a British beef farm: Grass. Fresh in summer, preserved as silage or hay in winter. This grass grew on land that cannot be cropped. Clover. Nitrogen-fixing. No synthetic fertiliser required where clover is present. Gerald eats the clover and deposits the nitrogen back into the soil in his manure. Hedge browsings. Hawthorn, hazel, field maple. Things a combine harvester has never and will never express an interest in. In winter, possibly: a modest quantity of brewers' grains: the spent barley from beer production that cannot be eaten by humans and would otherwise go to landfill or anaerobic digestion. Possibly some beet pulp: the fibrous residue from sugar processing. Indigestible to humans. Gerald converts it. Possibly some distillers' grains from whisky production. A by-product of an industry, converted to beef. The thought experiment is: what else do you do with this? The grass: you cannot eat it. You cannot process it into human food. You can leave it to grow, set seed, and decompose. The silage: same. The brewers' grains: landfill, biogas, or Gerald. The beet pulp: same. The hedgerow: same. Gerald is not competing with you for resources. Gerald is processing your waste, your margins, your by-products, and your non-arable land into beef and manure. The question is not "why are we feeding Gerald?" The question is "what were you planning to do with all of this without Gerald?"
